summary.overview: Five A1 grammar rules, one per page: the verb to be, subject pronouns, the articles a/an, possessive adjectives and the present simple. Each page gives the form, rules to remember, examples and practice.
summary.overview_ar: خمس قواعد للمستوى A1، قاعدة في كل صفحة: فعل الكينونة، الضمائر، أداتا a/an، صفات الملكية، والمضارع البسيط. لكل قاعدة جدول وأمثلة وتمارين.

topics.title: The verb "to be"
key_points: We use “to be” to say who someone is, how they feel, where they are and what something is like.
Negative: add not → I am not tired. She isn't at home. They aren't late.
Question: put the verb first → Are you a student? Is he your brother?
Short answers: Yes, I am. / No, she isn't.

topics.title: Subject pronouns
topics.title_ar: الضمائر: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
key_points: A subject pronoun takes the place of a name. It comes before the verb.
I is always a capital letter: Sara and I are friends.
Use it for things and animals: The book? It is on the table.
You is the same for one person and for many people.
examples: Omar is tall. → He is tall.
Lina and I are sisters. → We are sisters.
The phones are new. → They are new.

topics.title: Articles "a" and "an"
key_points: Use “a” or “an” before one thing (singular) that is not a specific one, or when we mention it for the first time.
Listen to the sound, not the letter: an hour (h is silent), a university (sounds like “you”).
Not with plurals: a cat → cats (not “a cats”).
Use “a/an” for jobs: She is a doctor. He is an engineer.

topics.title: Possessive adjectives
topics.title_ar: صفات الملكية: my, your, his, her…
key_points: Possessive adjectives show who something belongs to. They come before a noun: my book (not “book my”).
They never change for plural nouns: my book, my books.
Its (no apostrophe) = belongs to it. It's = it is.
Ask with whose: Whose bag is this? It's her bag.
examples: What's your name? My name is Rita.

topics.title: Present simple
topics.title_ar: المضارع البسيط: I like / she likes
key_points: Use the present simple for habits, routines and facts.
He / she / it → add -s: play → plays; -es after ch, sh, ss, x, o: watches, kisses, boxes, goes.
Consonant + y → -ies: study → studies. Special: have → has.
Time words: every day, usually, always, never, on Mondays.
